title: The Northstar Survey
design_status: Northstar Survey story authored around Team Lode copper/nickel extraction and its ICE ally's police impersonation, intimidation and kidnappings. The541-map shore successor preserves Winona New Game/starter/originals, Rochester delivery/Gym1, all eight city-bound gyms, Minneapolis ICE win/separate rescue/dispatch, St Paul courier/separate DEEP BORE manifest, Q06 foreman/cache/Grand Rapids handover, Duluth reveal, Q07 chief/receiver and Ryan's Baptism River cabin. Native roads now join the opening cities through St Cloud, Brainerd, the actual Leech Lake shore and Bemidji. Local continuous courses earn later badges, including a Pine loss/native clinic recovery/Fire-move retry and return. Controller, uncached preservation, actual stdio and audio checks pass for these slices. Prior badges/partners/RNG are explicit local setup; one earlier earned Care journey does not establish the current full campaign. Itasca/marker/Bemidji report/R09, Mankato Cut/cache, later regional and optional links, visited-only rail, League, Kettlurk and continuous fresh-start balance/retry remain unfinished. See STATUS.md, PROGRESSION.md and playable/leech-shore.md.
antagonist_motive: Team Lode and its ally Team ICE intend to drain the Boundary Waters to expose copper and nickel beneath the lakebeds. Lode steals survey instruments, falsifies warnings and plans to enslave Kettlurk to power the drainage pumps. Based in Minneapolis, Team ICE impersonates police, seizes evidence and threatens residents to protect the operation. Both leaderships understand the harm and choose extraction and control anyway. Lode covets the minerals; ICE actively wants the resulting destruction and displacement, and kidnaps anyone it suspects of opposition. Lode knowingly protects and benefits from those abductions.

quests.title: A field season begins
steps: Start upstairs; the guardian introduces the field station through page-by-page dialogue.
Choose CHIKORITA, CYNDAQUIL or TOTODILE at level 5.
Receive five POKE_BALL items and a parcel of original survey readings for Rochester, recorded by the existing parcel flag.
quests.repeat_guard: Never offer a second starter or repeat the item grant.
quests.failure: Canceling the starter choice leaves all choices available; starter is received before any route can open.

quests.title: The first station
steps: Cross Driftless Trail; optional farmer teaches grass and ledge use.
Deliver the original readings at the Rochester clinic. Matching station records and instruments have gone missing.
A Lode shipping stamp suggests a delivery error; deliberate theft is not yet proven.
Win the first gym and register the Care Badge.
quests.repeat_guard: Delivery text changes after handover; rewards are granted once.

quests.title: Prairie and river
steps: Recover the publicly reachable Mankato notebook: distant stations supposedly returned identical readings.
Win Mankato gym, travel through the river valley, and win Minneapolis gym.

Confront Team ICE in Minneapolis: Lode-paid bullies posing as police kidnap a rail dispatcher they suspect of opposition and seize the survey records. Win their enforcer battle, release the dispatcher through a separate interaction, then read the recovered dispatch copy; the crew remains hostile.
Read a rail dispatch note showing Team Lode diverted the missing instruments toward a northern pumping site.
quests.repeat_guard: Team ICE defeat comes only from an actual battle win. A separate dispatch reading sets its own flag; losses, refusals, repeats and Continue cannot bypass either interaction or duplicate rewards.

quests.title: Two cities one watershed
steps: Confront the Team Lode courier at the St Paul depot. He calls the diversion a correction, then threatens the player to identify who kept the originals delivered to Rochester.
Win the courier battle; the manifest identifies DEEP BORE. He remains hostile and loyal to Lode.
Win St Paul gym, return across the city crossing, and pass the north checkpoint with both Twin Cities badges.
Continue to St Cloud and win its gym.
quests.repeat_guard: Courier remains defeated and the northern gate stays open after save/reload.

quests.title: Lake country
steps: Win Brainerd gym and report at the ranger station. Fishers describe disrupted Pokemon habitats while the station reports insist nothing changed.
Receive the existing SURF field-move teaching item once; inherited badge permission still applies.
Reach Bemidji via the Leech Lake land route; Surf and lake side quests remain optional.
Win Bemidji gym; obtain an independent headwater reference to check the copied notebook values.
quests.repeat_guard: The teaching-item grant is once-only; no boating subsystem is introduced.

quests.title: Headwaters report
steps: Read the accessible dry-land headwaters marker at Lake Itasca.

Return to the Bemidji field officer. The independent reference and the officer's comparison copies expose one instrument log relabeled as multiple station surveys. The optional Mankato notebook is an earlier clue, not a required extra flag.
Investigate the tampered instruments on the Iron Range. The report does not claim Itasca drains into the northern mine.
quests.repeat_guard: The raw reading alone cannot open the Iron Range gate; the completed report does.

quests.title: The survey depot
steps: Investigate the stolen instruments in the Route 9 mine cache beside the fictional closed pumping site.
The Team Lode foreman admits the copper-nickel project will keep testing despite the warnings; defeat him in the reserved battle.

Separately inspect the guarded cache, confirm taking the survey meter and acknowledge the recovery text. Its saved recovery event carries the quest payload without inventing a bag item; declining remains retryable.
Return the recovered instrument to Grand Rapids; victory alone does not complete the handover.
Its records reveal pulse-pump tests and a northern control relay. Lode is deliberately driving a powerful Water Pokemon out of hiding.
quests.repeat_guard: Losing never grants the recovered instrument; after victory the foreman uses post-battle dialogue.

quests.title: North Shore signal
steps: Win Duluth gym for badge 8; bring the depot's copied meter log to the workshop receiver.

The harbor reveals the joint objective: Lode and ICE will drain the Boundary Waters for copper and nickel beneath the lakebeds. Lode intends to trap Kettlurk to power the pumps; ICE clears people and evidence out of the way. All eight badges and the harbor signal open North Shore travel.
Travel through Grand Marais and Gunflint. Keeper/fisher observations foreshadow a returning current; the local lamp repair remains its own quest.
At the free Boundary Waters shelter, confront the chief. He admits knowing the risks and choosing drainage anyway, with ICE protecting the operation. Win the existing boss battle.

Use the separate receiver. Declining remains retryable; confirming and acknowledging alignment restores the public line, sends the real readings and coordinates stopping the drainage pumps before the lakes are emptied. Safari fees and legendary capture never gate this scene.
quests.repeat_guard: No world flooding simulation. Local visual changes use saved block overrides; the story flag persists independently.
quests.safari_access_contract: The Safari preserve is optional wildlife play; entry fee, balls, step exhaustion and rare catches cannot block Q07 or passage to the League.

quests.title: The Ely League
steps: Traverse the reopened League trail and register at Ely; the survey is working while local recovery continues.
Defeat four successive League trainers and champion Casey through the authoritative battle engine.
Record the winning party through the existing Hall of Fame behavior.
Return for rematches and exploration. A future voluntary Kettlurk encounter is separate from champion completion.
quests.repeat_guard: A blackout resets the active League run without clearing badges, story completion or prior Hall of Fame entries.

quests.title: Three lake observations

Report to the Detroit Lakes ranger for one MAX_REPEL.
quests.repeat_guard: Reward once; not required for Q05.

quests.title: The prairie return
steps: Complete the optional prairie trainer circuit.
Read the Red River flood marker and return to the Moorhead depot for one NUGGET.
quests.repeat_guard: No west exit across the state border.

quests.title: Border ranger circuit
steps: Check in at the International Falls ranger desk.
After all badges and the harbor signal, traverse the optional Voyageurs loop to Boundary Waters.
Report the completed circuit for one PP_UP.
quests.repeat_guard: The side loop cannot bypass the Q07 flag at the League approach.

quests.title: Mille Lacs shore watch
steps: Speak to the three shore-watch volunteers using walking access.
Return to the dock ranger for an existing fishing-rod upgrade chosen after checking base-pack item IDs.

narrative.tone: A local mystery that grows into a Pokemon adventure. Villains have credible motives, professional competence and distinct personalities, but knowingly choose harmful means. No cartoon greed speeches, sympathetic absolution, redeemed courier or claim that the player and Team Lode are equally right.
narrative.logline: An ordinary delivery preserves the readings Team Lode needs erased. Follow the missing instruments north, expose its alliance with Minneapolis police impersonators Team ICE, and stop them draining the Boundary Waters for copper and nickel.
narrative.player_stake: The player personally delivers the original records and meets the people and Pokemon who depend on the surveyed places. The courier later demands to know who kept those records. The opening errand preserves the evidence that undoes the scheme; the delivered parcel is not secretly still in the player's bag.
narrative.public_cover: Team Lode sells its DEEP BORE project as dependable work and essential metal. Its leaders use that promise to conceal risk, silence witnesses and keep their investment moving. Honest mine workers may oppose the scheme; occupation and hometown do not make someone a villain.
narrative.true_plan: Team Lode and Team ICE want to drain the Boundary Waters to reach minerals beneath the lakebeds. Lode builds a fictional network of pulse pumps and intends to trap Kettlurk, forcing its returning current to power the drainage. ICE protects shipments and equipment, seizes records and drives residents and witnesses away under fraudulent police authority. Both leaders know the project will destroy the lakes and habitat; the falsified surveys are deliberate concealment. The operation is interrupted before the lakes are emptied. ICE welcomes destruction and displacement as a way to break resistance. Its crew kidnaps anyone it thinks is against it, without requiring evidence. Lode knowingly shields the kidnappings to keep its operation running.

legendary.name: Kettlurk
legendary.role: Intended captive, never the cause of the cover-up or a willing villain. Reports of a disappearing and returning current foreshadow its identity.
legendary.main_story_requirement: Stop Lode without catching, defeating, owning or registering Kettlurk. A later voluntary encounter stays on the existing optional Devil's Kettle branch near Grand Marais.
legendary.implementation_status: Authored roster design, not a compiled encounter. A future apparition and machine set piece require native art/scripts. Current Q07 dialogue can identify the intended captive without inventing a runtime encounter.

cast_arcs.role: Connects the ordinary field assignment to the falsified data; coordinates public reporting and gives concrete tasks. The original readings matter more than a final lecture.

Controlled and evasive. Calls the stolen equipment a shipping correction, then threatens the player to identify the keeper of the delivered originals. After losing, gives up the manifest but remains loyal to Lode.
Practical and intimidating. Knows instruments were tampered with and workers are at risk; orders the next test anyway. Sees Pokemon as replaceable equipment.

Head of Team Lode, occupying a public survey shelter. Believes he alone can decide what the region must sacrifice for his project. Understands the evidence and deliberately suppresses it. Defeat costs him control; it does not produce repentance.

narrative.ending: The chief battle clears access to the occupied relay. A separate receiver action restores the public link, transmits the real readings and drainage plan, and coordinates crews stopping the drainage pumps before the lakes are emptied or Kettlurk is trapped. The alliance loses control of the operation; neither team is redeemed. Survey work and the Ely trail resume while damage assessment and local recovery continue. No instant refilling, purification or compulsory legendary capture.
narrative.geography_rule: Itasca is an independent reference used to expose copied records, not evidence that its water flows to the mine or Boundary Waters. Distinct basins stay distinct; Kettlurk's returning current and pulse machinery are explicitly fantasy.

sources.use: Distinguish iron/taconite from nonferrous copper and nickel. Team Lode and its project are fictional.
Background for water-quality baseline surveys in copper-nickel-bearing sulfide terrain; not evidence for any fictional wrongdoing or supernatural hydrology.

narrative.reference_fallback: The Bemidji officer keeps comparison copies of the station records and equipment manifest. Q05 can expose a duplicated instrument log without requiring the optional Mankato notebook flag. Finding that notebook gives the player an earlier clue, not a new progression gate.

allied_antagonists.name: Team ICE
allied_antagonists.relationship: Team ICE is Team Lode's willing ally in draining the Boundary Waters. Lode wants the exposed minerals; ICE wants the destruction, displacement and control the operation enables. Lode finances the pumps and enforcement work and knowingly shields ICE's kidnappings; ICE supplies intimidation, seized records and fraudulent police authority.
allied_antagonists.direction: Openly cruel bullies impersonating police. They use counterfeit badges and invented inspection powers to seize survey records, threaten residents and protect Lode shipments. Their claimed authority is fraudulent; losing does not reform them. Keep their language terse and abusive, with no ice puns or comic incompetence. Their leadership knows the drainage objective and protects it deliberately; they are accountable partners in the scheme.
allied_antagonists.native_status: Native Minneapolis battle, separate rescue/reading, return home and canonical Avrin gym are verified on the integrated 515-map city-story candidate. Regional arrival and the full earned journey remain open. See playable/minneapolis.md.
allied_antagonists.motive: ICE actively wants the destruction the drainage would cause: emptied lakes, displaced residents and broken resistance. Its leaders treat destroying a place people defend as a demonstration of power. They kidnap anybody they suspect of opposing them; evidence of actual resistance is unnecessary. Express this through grounded threats, seizures, disappearances and coercion, with restrained dialogue rather than gleeful cartoon speeches.
allied_antagonists.kidnapping_contract: ICE abducts people based on suspicion alone, including residents, workers, witnesses and trainers. Show the consequences in missing-person accounts, frightened witnesses and recoverable captives. The Minneapolis dispatcher is held at the rail dispatch site; an actual enforcer win opens a separate release interaction before the recovered dispatch copy is read. A loss cannot release the captive; repeats and Continue cannot duplicate the rescue or rewards. Native placement, battle win/loss, custody/release, physical departure, separate reading, repeat and Continue are verified on the integrated candidate. Regional progression remains incomplete.
